text: each lens was mounted to an ARAMIS 12M, 12 Megapixel sensor. The two sensor-lens assemblies were mounted on an adjustable bar so that the camera distance was 100 mm. The working measurement distance to the bend specimen was 314 mm. The angle between the two optical camera axes was 25°. Using this configuration, the system was calibrated using the cp40/60/21391 calibration panel, which resulted in a calibrated measurement volume of 65 mm long, 45 mm wide, and 30 mm deep. Where the long edge of the volume was perpendicular to the bend axis and the center of the volume coincided with the midpoint of the bend specimen. The calibration deviation (epipolar error) was 0.060 pixels. Further the region of interest (ROI) was defined as rectangular area about 21 mm wide spanning the width of the specimen and about 4 mm high. The ROI was centered at the midpoint of the bend specimen. This ROI was chosen to exclude the near edge regions of the specimens and capture true plain strain behavior in the center region of the specimen. A random speckle pattern was applied to the center of the bend specimens. This was done in a similar way as above by first masking the specimens, then spraying painting them with a flat white spray paint, following by applying a black speckles using flat black spray paint, removing mask so that the ROI was covered in a random speckle patter. During three point bend testing images were captured at a rate of 20 Hz with a ring buffer of 260. Frames prior to the last 260 were captured at a reduced rate of 5 Hz. Collected DIC images were processed using a facet size of 21 pixels and a point distance of 8 pixels. This resulted in 3-5 features per facet, resulting in a pixel resolution of ~25μm/pixel. Facet matching was done against the previous stage for the collected image sequence. The center of the facets corresponded to nodes of a triangular mesh. The full 3D displacement field was then measured throughout the test. Equivalent plastic strain was then computed from the displacement measurements. The fracture initiation stage was then visually identified by the user. This was done by first identifying the largest crack to occur in the test. Once the largest crack was identified the user worked backwards in the DIC image sequence until the largest crack fully closed. Then working forwards the first opening of this largest crack was visually identified. An opening was defined as a region of separated paint just exposing the metal substrate. This first opening was typically less than 21 pixels (facet length). The image frame just prior to the first opening was selected as the fracture initiation stage. Then a script was used to (1) label the selected point as the fracture initiation point; (2) draw multiple square regions around the point. The square regions were 0.250, 0.500, 1.000, and 2.000 mm in length. In each square region the average major strain, average minor strain, and average effective plastic strain was computed.
